kultivator.kota_besar.arena.inspired: Source: Inspired by the lei tai platforms where fighters of old China answered challenges; game design.
kultivator.kota_besar.balai_tabib.inspir: Source: Inspired by the Benevolent Pharmacies (Huimin Ju) the Song government set up to sell cheap medicine, and by the healing halls of sects in cultivation novels; game design.
kultivator.kota_besar.dermaga_langit.ins: Source: Inspired by the flying ships and spirit boats of cultivation novels, and the busy quays of Kaifeng in the painting "Along the River During the Qingming Festival"; game design.
kultivator.kota_besar.gelombang_binatang: Source: Inspired by the beast tides (shou chao) that assault cities in many xianxia novels; game design.
kultivator.kota_besar.gerbang.inspired: Source: Inspired by the curfew of Tang dynasty Chang'an: the street drums beaten at dusk closed the city gates and its wards, which opened again at dawn; game design.
kultivator.kota_besar.gilda_alkemis.insp: Source: Inspired by the Alchemist Association and the Pill Meeting of Battle Through the Heavens; game design.
kultivator.kota_besar.gilda_kultivator.i: Source: Inspired by the hunters' guilds with ranked mission boards and the rankings of young prodigies that appear in many xianxia novels; game design.
kultivator.kota_besar.gilda_tempa.inspir: Source: Inspired by Ou Yezi, the Spring and Autumn period swordsmith who in legend forged the Zhanlu and Longyuan swords, and by the artifact forges of cultivation novels; game design.
kultivator.kota_besar.hari_gerbang.inspi: Source: Inspired by the spirit-root tests and sect recruitment days of A Record of a Mortal's Journey to Immortality and other cultivation novels; game design.
kultivator.kota_besar.judi_batu.inspired: Source: Inspired by the source-stone gambling of Shrouded the Heavens (Zhe Tian) by Chen Dong; game design.
kultivator.kota_besar.kuil_langit.inspir: Source: Inspired by the Hall of the Three Pure Ones (Sanqing) of Taoist temples and the great incense burners in their courtyards; game design.
kultivator.kota_besar.lelang_agung.inspi: Source: Inspired by the Mittel Auction House of Battle Through the Heavens and the treasure auctions of many cultivation novels; game design.
kultivator.kota_besar.pasar_binatang.ins: Source: Inspired by the bird-and-flower markets of old Chinese cities and the trade in spirit beast cubs in xianxia novels; game design.
kultivator.kota_besar.pasar_malam.inspir: Source: Inspired by the night markets of Song dynasty Kaifeng that stayed open until the small hours, as recorded in "Dongjing Meng Hua Lu"; game design.
kultivator.kota_besar.penginapan.inspire: Source: Inspired by the inns (kezhan) of wuxia stories, where swordsmen meet, quarrel and hear the news; game design.
kultivator.kota_besar.perpustakaan.inspi: Source: Inspired by the Tianyi Pavilion in Ningbo, the oldest surviving private library in China (Ming dynasty), and by the scripture pavilions of sects in cultivation novels; game design.
kultivator.kota_besar.pertemuan_pil.insp: Source: Inspired by the Pill Meeting (Dan Hui) of Battle Through the Heavens by Tian Can Tu Dou; game design.
kultivator.kota_besar.pertemuan_sekte.in: Source: Inspired by the gatherings of school leaders in wuxia stories, such as the Five Mountains Sword Alliance meeting on Mount Song in The Smiling, Proud Wanderer by Jin Yong; game design.
kultivator.kota_besar.rumah_makan.inspir: Source: Inspired by the eating houses of Song dynasty Kaifeng described by Meng Yuanlao in "Dongjing Meng Hua Lu"; game design.
kultivator.kota_besar.rumah_uang.inspire: Source: Inspired by the "flying money" (feiqian) of the Tang dynasty, notes that could be cashed in another city, and the money houses (qianzhuang) of the Ming and Qing; game design.
kultivator.kota_besar.stasiun_teleport.i: Source: Inspired by the ancient teleportation arrays of A Record of a Mortal's Journey to Immortality (Fanren Xiuxian Zhuan) by Wang Yu and other cultivation novels; game design.
kultivator.kota_besar.toko_senjata.inspi: Source: Inspired by the smiths' streets and weapon shops of wuxia stories, where swordsmen choose a blade before setting out; game design.
kultivator.kota_besar.turnamen_agung.ins: Source: Inspired by the lei tai platforms of old China and the inter-sect tournaments of xianxia novels; game design.
kultivator.kota_besar.yamen.inspired: Source: Inspired by the Kaifeng prefecture office (yamen) where Judge Bao Zheng held court, and the grievance drum (dengwen gu) commoners could beat to ask for justice; game design.
kultivator.lore.gilda.alkemis.1: Forty years ago a plague swept the capital. The skin of the sick turned yellow as autumn leaves, and within seven days they stopped breathing. The sect alchemists refused to come; no sect wanted its disciples infected in a city it did not own.
kultivator.lore.gilda.alkemis.2: A young guild alchemist named Dan Chen did not sleep for nineteen days and brewed his first formula from a root used to dye cloth. It saved half the city. He became Guild Head at an age that made the elders jealous, and he has never forgiven himself for the other half.
kultivator.lore.gilda.alkemis.3: Since then the Alchemist Guild must keep a stock of antidote pills for the whole city, and every alchemist who passes the guild exam swears to come when a plague comes, wherever it is. The weekly Pill Gathering is the guild's way of finding new hands calm enough for that oath.
kultivator.lore.gilda.alkemis.judul: The Alchemist Guild: The Yellow Leaf Plague
kultivator.lore.gilda.kultivator.1: This guild was founded by spirit beast hunters too wild for the sects and too strong for the villages. They sold beast cores at the old road post, and when the city wall was raised, they were the first called to guard it. The guild's mission board was once a single tiger hide pinned with the names of beasts.
kultivator.lore.gilda.kultivator.2: Twenty years ago the greatest Beast Tide in the city's memory struck the east wall. A young hunter named Lin Fei held a breach in the wall all night; at dawn he had lost his left arm and a bone tiger lay dead at his feet. He became Guild Head that same year.
kultivator.lore.gilda.kultivator.3: Today the guild records the hundred finest young cultivators on the Young Dragon List and gives starred badges to anyone who finishes its missions. Lin Fei says the badge is not an honour but a sign that the guild knows where to look for your body.
kultivator.lore.gilda.kultivator.judul: The Cultivators' Guild: Hunters Who Settled
kultivator.lore.gilda.pandai.1: The masters of this guild claim descent from the students of Ou Ye, a swordsmith of a very old age who, it is said, forged five famous swords from iron worked by water, fire and patience. No one knows whether the lineage is true. The smiths do not care; they say a lineage is proven on the anvil, not on paper.
kultivator.lore.gilda.pandai.2: Every new master must forge one nameless sword and give it to the guild. Those swords hang in the guild hall by the hundreds, and it is said that on certain nights one of them rings by itself when the owner it waits for passes in the street.
kultivator.lore.gilda.pandai.3: The master who leads the guild now is called Ou Ye the Younger. He hates the name and forges harder because of it.
kultivator.lore.gilda.pandai.judul: The Forge Guild: The Students of Ou Ye
kultivator.lore.gilda.pandai.sumber: Source: Inspired by Ou Yezi, the legendary swordsmith of the state of Yue in the Spring and Autumn period who, according to the Yue Jue Shu, forged swords such as Zhanlu and Chunjun; the line of students and this guild are game design.
kultivator.lore.gua.cermin_hati.1: In damp forests lies a small cave with a pool whose water never ripples. It reflects not faces but intentions: whoever sits by it long enough sees their own heart demon standing on the water.
kultivator.lore.gua.cermin_hati.2: A monk once saw his demon in a pool like this and laughed until he wept, for it wore the face of his mother scolding him for never coming home. He later became the teacher of Monk Jing Xin at the capital temple, and taught that a heart demon is not defeated but recognised.
kultivator.lore.gua.cermin_hati.judul: Heart Mirror Caves: Pools that Reflect Intent
kultivator.lore.gua.makam.1: Great ancestors who died without students sometimes built tombs beneath the earth and left a remnant of their soul inside. The door is only a stele in open country; beneath it a painted corridor tells the ancestor's life to anyone strong enough to descend.
kultivator.lore.gua.makam.2: Three trial rooms guard the inheritance: Heart, Strength and Comprehension. The remnant soul does not seek the strongest, but the one most like its own young self. Many pass two trials and go home empty-handed, having failed a question the ancestor never could answer either.
kultivator.lore.gua.makam.3: Once the inheritance is given the remnant soul finally rests. The tomb remains, silent, and heirs sometimes return to light incense in the empty hall.
kultivator.lore.gua.makam.judul: Inheritance Tombs: Doors that Wait for an Heir
kultivator.lore.gua.pertapa.1: On quiet slopes some strong cultivators choose to live alone: a patch of herbs beneath a light shaft, a spring, one room for meditation. They seek no students, but sometimes accept one person patient enough for their three trials.
kultivator.lore.gua.pertapa.2: After passing on their art, hermits usually leave to wander and do not return. The cave they leave behind makes a fine abode for whoever inherits it, for its qi has been tamed by decades of meditation.
kultivator.lore.gua.pertapa.judul: Hermit Caves: Those Who Left the World
kultivator.lore.gua.pertapa.tabel.0: Why this cave's hermit left the world: the student he loved most killed a fellow disciple over one pill. He did not punish him; he simply left, because he no longer knew what he had truly been teaching.
kultivator.lore.gua.pertapa.tabel.1: Why this cave's hermit left the world: she won every duel for three hundred years and one morning realised she could not remember a single opponent's face.
kultivator.lore.gua.pertapa.tabel.2: Why this cave's hermit left the world: his mortal wife died of old age while he still looked thirty. He planted a plum tree before the cave, her favourite, and tends it every day.
kultivator.lore.gua.pertapa.tabel.3: Why this cave's hermit left the world: her sect was destroyed in one night while she sat in closed meditation. She emerged a hundred years later and found no one left to avenge.
kultivator.lore.gua.pertapa.tabel.4: Why this cave's hermit left the world: he lost a wager to a monk and must stay on the mountain until he can answer one question. The monk is long dead. The question is still unanswered.
kultivator.lore.gua.pertapa.tabel.5: Why this cave's hermit left the world: she was bored. That is all, she says, and laughs every time someone looks for a deeper reason.
kultivator.lore.gua.pertapa.tabel.6: Why this cave's hermit left the world: he was nearly overtaken by his heart demon in battle and killed innocent people. He exiled himself so no one would be near him if it happened again.
kultivator.lore.gua.pertapa.tabel.7: Why this cave's hermit left the world: she heard a certain herb blooms only once in five hundred years on this slope and decided to wait. It has bloomed once. She decided to wait again.
kultivator.lore.gua.pertapa.tabel.8: Why this cave's hermit left the world: the emperor of a mortal kingdom asked him to be his war adviser. He refused and hid here, and that kingdom has fallen twice since.
kultivator.lore.gua.pertapa.tabel.9: Why this cave's hermit left the world: she wanted to know whether the Dao can be understood without a teacher, a book or a rival. After two centuries she says the answer is "almost", and she is still looking for the rest.
kultivator.lore.gua.sarang_binatang.1: A spirit beast that lives long enough absorbs the earth's qi until its body changes: its fangs harden like iron, its eyes remember, and it begins to gather other beasts around it. Its den may be a cave, or a giant tree with a hollow trunk.
kultivator.lore.gua.sarang_binatang.2: The hunters of the Cultivators' Guild say a beast den is the best school for a tamed spirit beast: those that fight here grow faster. They also say every den has a mother, and the young she leaves behind sometimes wander and can be tamed by a patient hand.
kultivator.lore.gua.sarang_iblis.1: Behind ordinary-looking cliffs the demonic path's cultivators dig their lairs: a hall of blood pools, cells for captives, rooms for forbidden pills. They abduct mortals from roads and villages, for human blood and souls are ingredients no market sells.
kultivator.lore.gua.sarang_iblis.2: People say lairs like this are branches of %s, or of disciples it cast out. The sect has never admitted it, nor ever denied it. The demon elder who rules a lair usually fears his own sect more than any hero.
kultivator.lore.gua.sarang_iblis.3: Freed captives must be escorted to safety; the road home is more dangerous than the lair, for demon hunters hate losing their ingredients.
kultivator.lore.gua.sarang_iblis.sumber: Source: Inspired by the strongholds of demonic-path cultivators who abduct mortals for their brews, a common xianxia trope; the lairs and their dwellers are game design.
kultivator.lore.gua.urat_roh.1: Deep underground the earth's qi flows like a river and sometimes crystallises into purple and white walls that glow of themselves. Miners call it a spirit vein; village elders call it the dragon's breath.
kultivator.lore.gua.urat_roh.2: Myth says a dragon sleeps beneath the whole continent, its body the mountain ranges. These crystal grottoes are where its scales crack, and the qi leaking from them calls rare treasures to be born nearby. The crystal guardians who stand in these caves, people say, are flakes of scale that learned to walk.
kultivator.lore.gua.urat_roh.judul: Spirit Vein Grottoes: Where the Dragon Sleeps
kultivator.lore.gua.urat_roh.sumber: Source: Inspired by the dragon veins (longmai) of Chinese fengshui, the flow of earth qi that follows mountain ranges; the sleeping dragon and the crystal guardians are game design.
kultivator.lore.jalan.dagang.1: At busy crossroads merchants built caravanserais: an inner courtyard ringed by storerooms and chambers, with one gate locked at night. Caravans from many lands meet here and trade goods that cannot be found at home.
kultivator.lore.jalan.dagang.2: The caravanserai's law is older than any city's: whoever has passed the gate is a guest, even your enemy, and no one draws a weapon in the courtyard. A merchant who breaks that law will never again be received at any caravanserai along the road.
kultivator.lore.jalan.dagang.sumber: Source: Inspired by the caravanserais along the Silk Road, courtyard inns where caravans rested and traded; its law of guests is game design.
kultivator.lore.jalan.kemah_begal.1: Some dozens of paces from the road, hidden behind trees, bandits pitch camps with sharpened palisades and campfires never lit while a caravan is near. Most are farmers who lost their fields, expelled disciples, or failed cultivators who cannot face their villages.
kultivator.lore.jalan.kemah_begal.2: The Cultivators' Guild posts a mission for every known camp. The hunters say the most dangerous bandit is not the strongest, but the one who still has something to protect.
kultivator.lore.jalan.kemah_begal.sumber: Source: Inspired by the highway robbers of the Water Margin (Shuihu Zhuan) who waylaid convoys on mountain roads; the camps and their dwellers are game design.
kultivator.lore.jalan.kuil.1: Along the roads stand little shrines, no taller than a man, for the Earth God who guards travellers. He is no mighty god; he is the god who remembers everyone who passes and makes sure they arrive.
kultivator.lore.jalan.kuil.2: Those who light a stick of incense here feel their steps lighter for a while. Old wanderers say it is not magic, only the relief of being heard. They light the incense anyway.
kultivator.lore.jalan.kuil.judul: Road Shrines: The Travellers' Earth God
kultivator.lore.jalan.kuil.sumber: Source: Inspired by the small roadside shrines of Tudi Gong (the Earth God) at Chinese roadsides and village entrances; the Road Blessing is game design.
kultivator.lore.jalan.penyeberangan.1: At rivers too wide to bridge, the road stops at a small dock and continues at the dock across. Between them is only a raft and a ferryman who takes one spirit stone from every passenger, cultivator or not.
kultivator.lore.jalan.penyeberangan.2: The ferrymen have a saying: "On the water everyone weighs the same." Even masters who can fly are said to ride the raft now and then just to hear the ferryman talk, for a ferryman knows the news of both banks.
kultivator.lore.jalan.singgah.1: Long ago these posts were the Road King's courier stations: where horses were changed and letters passed on, so news could cross hundreds of li in a few days. The kingdom is long gone, but the posts live on, sold from one owner to the next.
kultivator.lore.jalan.singgah.2: Today a waystation is the best place to hear news. Wanderers, guild couriers and peddlers trade stories in the eatery while waiting for the rain to stop. The great posts at crossroads even have formation discs linked to the capital's stations.
kultivator.lore.jalan.singgah.sumber: Source: Inspired by the relay posts (yizhan) of the Chinese imperial roads, which in the Tang dynasty stood roughly every thirty li; the waystations and their discs are game design.
kultivator.lore.jalan.tonggak.1: Every five hundred horse paces along the old roads stands a carved stone post. Its carving gives the distance in li to the places at both ends of the road and, beneath it, nearly worn away, the name of the Road King: an ancient mortal ruler who ordered that every road in his land be readable even by those who could not read.
kultivator.lore.jalan.tonggak.2: Merchants have a habit of touching every milestone they pass; a road once touched, they say, will not lead you astray. Old caravan maps were drawn from milestone to milestone, not town to town.
kultivator.lore.jalan.tonggak.judul: Road Milestones: Stones that Count the Li
kultivator.lore.jalan.tonggak.sumber: Source: Inspired by the li, the old Chinese unit of distance, the roadside distance mounds (hou) of the Tang dynasty raised every five and ten li, and the straight roads of the Qin dynasty; the Road King is game design.
kultivator.lore.kampung.1: Mortal villages live in the shadow of the sect mountains. They plant rice, keep livestock and marry off their children like villages anywhere, but every family knows a tale of a neighbour's child taken away one day by a white-robed cultivator and returned fifty years later not a day older.
kultivator.lore.kampung.2: This village, like most in its land, has a long history with %s: sometimes protected, sometimes taxed, sometimes forgotten. The elders keep a list of the village children who ever passed that sect's trial behind the Earth God's altar, and read the names aloud on New Year's Eve.
kultivator.lore.kampung.3: The bell on the village square is not only a clock. When a village swears loyalty to a sect, that sect's plaque hangs on the bell post, and from that day the village pays rice and sends its gifted children, while the sect promises to come when beasts or bandits come. The second promise is broken more often than the first.
kultivator.lore.kampung.judul: Mortal Villages Below the Sect Mountains
kultivator.lore.kampung.klan.1: A clan village is no ordinary village. Its walls are high, its young train from the day they can walk, and everyone in it bears one family name. Cultivator clans live between the mortal world and the sect world: too small to be a sect, too proud to bow to any.
kultivator.lore.kampung.klan.2: In the Ancestral Hall the spirit tablets run from the founding ancestor to the last who fell. Each new tablet is written with blood from the patriarch's fingertip, and every gifted clan child is brought there on their seventh birthday to be introduced to the ancestors. A child who cries is thought to be favoured.
kultivator.lore.kampung.klan.judul: Clan Villages: Blood and Ancestral Tablets
kultivator.lore.kampung.klan.sumber: Source: Inspired by the ancestral halls (citang) of Chinese clans with their spirit tablets, and by cultivator clans such as the Xiao family of Battle Through the Heavens; the clan origins are game design.
kultivator.lore.kampung.klan.tabel.0: This clan's origin: its ancestor was a bodyguard who saved a sect master and refused to join, then received this land as reward. The clan still keeps his blunted sword above the altar.
kultivator.lore.kampung.klan.tabel.1: This clan's origin: three brothers found a small spirit vein under the family well and swore never to sell it. Two hundred years later the well became the heart of the village, and the oath became clan law.
kultivator.lore.kampung.klan.tabel.2: This clan's origin: its ancestor was an expelled disciple cast out for stealing a manual. He never returned it, and it became the clan's inherited art. His old sect still asks for it back every hundred years.
kultivator.lore.kampung.klan.tabel.3: This clan's origin: it was once a family of salt merchants who hired cultivators to guard their caravans. A generation later they stopped hiring and began to train themselves.
kultivator.lore.kampung.klan.tabel.4: This clan's origin: its founder was a woman who married a spirit beast in human form, the tale says. Clan members are said never to be bitten by snakes, and they do not deny the tale.
kultivator.lore.kampung.klan.tabel.5: This clan's origin: its ancestor was a palace cook who brought home one pill recipe from an alchemist's kitchen. The clan is now known for its pills, and for its food.
kultivator.lore.kampung.klan.tabel.6: This clan's origin: the clan survived the war of the seven sects by hiding in a cave for seven years. Each year they fast for seven days to remember it, and no guest is fed that week.
kultivator.lore.kampung.klan.tabel.7: This clan's origin: the first patriarch beat a sect's young master in a duel and won this land as the stake. Since then every young master of the clan is expected to challenge anyone passing through, a custom that made the clan famous and often embarrassed.
kultivator.lore.kampung.sumber: Source: Inspired by Tudi Gong, the local Earth God with a small shrine in nearly every Chinese village, and by Han Li's home village in the mountains at the start of A Record of a Mortal's Journey to Immortality; the village legends are game design.
kultivator.lore.kampung.tabel.0: This village's legend: its Earth God was once a farmer who stopped a flood with his own body. Each rainy season the villagers leave a new pair of straw sandals at his shrine, so he need not walk barefoot while guarding the dyke.
kultivator.lore.kampung.tabel.1: This village's legend: the well on the square is called the Lucky Well. Whoever draws the first water on New Year's Day will be lucky all year, so the young men sleep beside it the night before and wake up shoving one another.
kultivator.lore.kampung.tabel.10: This village's legend: in a great drought a wandering healer dug a well with his staff and left without asking payment. Its water is bitter but has never run dry, and the villagers call it the Healer's Water.
kultivator.lore.kampung.tabel.11: This village's legend: a spirit fox once lived in the bamboo behind the village and traded stolen chickens for mushrooms that cure fever. Every house still leaves one egg on the fence on full-moon nights, just in case.
kultivator.lore.kampung.tabel.2: This village's legend: sixty years ago the river burst and carried off half the houses. A turtle as large as a table rose and bore the headman's baby on its back to the hill, then went back into the water. No one here eats turtle.
kultivator.lore.kampung.tabel.3: This village's legend: the old tree at the end of the road was planted by a cultivator who stopped to ask for water. He said it would blossom in the year the village bore a child with a spirit root. It has blossomed three times.
kultivator.lore.kampung.tabel.4: This village's legend: its Earth God is famously forgetful. The villagers write their wishes on red paper and paste them on the shrine wall, so he can read them again when he forgets.
kultivator.lore.kampung.tabel.5: This village's legend: on foggy nights a gong sounds from the hill, though there is no temple there. The elders say it is a village guard from the war of the seven sects still at his post, and children are forbidden to answer if their name is called.
kultivator.lore.kampung.tabel.6: This village's legend: no rat has ever entered the village granary, because a calico cat that lives there is over a hundred years old. It does not like to be touched, and twice it has been seen walking on the paddy water.
kultivator.lore.kampung.tabel.7: This village's legend: seven families fleeing a war founded the village. They carried seven stones from their old homes and buried them under the bell post. As long as the stones stay there, people say, no founding family will die out.
kultivator.lore.kampung.tabel.8: This village's legend: a bride from this village once refused to marry a sect's young master, fled into the mountains and came back an elder of another sect. The young master, people say, still does not dare pass this way.
kultivator.lore.kampung.tabel.9: This village's legend: each harvest the Earth God borrows one sack of rice and returns it twice over the next year. No one has ever seen who takes the sack, but no one has ever stopped leaving it.
kultivator.lore.kompleks.1: Behind a sect's gate the mountain is divided like a stair: the outer disciples' court at the foot, the inner disciples' hall on the slope, the master's hall at the peak. A disciple spends years climbing a single terrace. To outsiders the gate and the peak are a few hundred steps apart; to a disciple they are a lifetime.
kultivator.lore.kompleks.2: Guests are treated by how your sect stands with %s. Allies and friends are welcomed as far as the inner hall and may spar in the training court; neutral guests only reach the court; enemies are warned at the gate. In war the same mountain becomes a fortress, and every step is guarded.
kultivator.lore.kompleks.judul: Sect Compounds: Court, Inner Hall, Peak
kultivator.lore.kompleks.sumber: Source: Inspired by the Seven Mysteries Sect of A Record of a Mortal's Journey to Immortality and the Reliance Sect of I Shall Seal the Heavens: an outer disciples' court, an inner disciples' peak, a hall at the summit; the founders' tales are game design.
kultivator.lore.kompleks.tabel.0: The disciples say the founder of %s cut a mountain in two with one stroke, then built the main hall in the cleft so the disciples would remember that nothing is impossible for a sincere blade.
kultivator.lore.kompleks.tabel.1: The disciples say the founder of %s was a shepherd boy who fell asleep in a cave and dreamed a god taught him for a hundred years. When he woke only one night had passed, and he had already formed a Golden Core.
kultivator.lore.kompleks.tabel.10: The disciples say the founder of %s drove a flood dragon from this valley and bound its tailbone under the bell tower. When the bell rings by itself, the dragon is dreaming.
kultivator.lore.kompleks.tabel.11: The disciples say the founder of %s never wrote a single word. Every manual of the sect was written by students from memory, and each differs a little from the others. The elders say the differences are the true teaching.
kultivator.lore.kompleks.tabel.2: The disciples say the founder of %s traded her eyes to a mountain spirit for a manual, and from then on saw qi instead of light. That is why the sect's elders train blindfolded once a year.
kultivator.lore.kompleks.tabel.3: The disciples say the founder of %s was a cook who reached enlightenment stirring porridge. The wooden ladle still hangs in the main hall, and every new disciple must serve three months in the kitchen.
kultivator.lore.kompleks.tabel.4: The disciples say the founder of %s defied heaven itself and withstood nine tribulation strikes under a paper umbrella. The umbrella burned; he did not. Disciples carry paper umbrellas when they break through, for luck.
kultivator.lore.kompleks.tabel.5: The disciples say the founder of %s came to this mountain chasing a white crane that stole his manual, and never left. The cranes around the peak are protected by sect law.
kultivator.lore.kompleks.tabel.6: The disciples say the founder of %s defeated seven sects in seven days, then refused all he had won except the stone he sat on. That stone is still the sect master's seat.
kultivator.lore.kompleks.tabel.7: The disciples say the founder of %s planted one lotus seed in the peak pool, and the lotus has not wilted in a thousand years. If it ever wilts, the prophecy says, the sect will fall.
kultivator.lore.kompleks.tabel.8: The disciples say the founders of %s were two friends who argued over one technique for forty years and finally founded a sect so they could keep arguing in peace. The sect still has two branches that mock each other.
kultivator.lore.kompleks.tabel.9: The disciples say the founder of %s climbed this mountain carrying his sick mother, seeking a herb said to grow at the peak. She was cured, and the herb garden in the court is the garden he planted for her.
kultivator.lore.kota_besar.1: Nine hundred years ago this plain was a battlefield. Seven sects fought for three generations until the rivers ran the colour of rust and no farmer dared to sow. In the winter of the fortieth year the sect masters met in the ruins of a road post, because it was the only place no one owned.
kultivator.lore.kota_besar.2: They signed no treaty. They broke their own swords, planted them in the stone and raised a wall around it. The city's first law was carved above the gate: "Within the walls, swords sleep." The city has no king. The Pavilion of the City Guard keeps it in the name of every sect, and its Warden Prince is chosen by the guild council, not born.
kultivator.lore.kota_besar.3: Because no sect may own it, everyone comes here: merchants afraid of bandits, alchemists in need of buyers, expelled disciples looking for work, and old cultivators weary of grudges. The city grew from one square into nine districts within the walls, with a slum and a caravan field clinging to the outside like moss on a stone.
kultivator.lore.kota_besar.4: The oath has been broken many times, and each time the city has claimed its blood. Yet every sect knows that whoever seizes the capital will have the other six as enemies at once. The peace here was not born of kindness but of arithmetic. The merchants say that is the most durable kind.
kultivator.lore.kota_besar.arena.1: A hundred years after the oath two sects nearly went to war again over a spirit vein. The Warden Prince of the day offered another way: each sect would send one champion, and the loser would give up its claim. The whole city watched the bout, and both sects went home with no one dead.
kultivator.lore.kota_besar.arena.2: Since then sect disputes have been settled on the arena stage, not the battlefield. The Grand Inter-Sect Tournament grew from that custom. The crowd cheers, the bookmakers bet, and the elders are quietly relieved: every champion who loses here is a hundred disciples who do not die out there.
kultivator.lore.kota_besar.arena.judul: The Grand Arena: A Bout, Not a War
kultivator.lore.kota_besar.arena.sumber: Source: Inspired by the lei tai, the raised platform on which Chinese martial artists fought to settle disputes or test their art; the Grand Arena and its history are game design.
kultivator.lore.kota_besar.awan.1: Two hundred years ago the first spirit ship came down over the capital, steered by a drunken and very lucky elder. It caught on the roof of a cloth seller's house. The guild council bought the house, pulled it down and built a dock on the same spot, because "the sky had chosen".
kultivator.lore.kota_besar.awan.2: Today the Sky Dock serves cloud boats to distant places, and the cloud captains have become a people of their own: tanned by the high sun, sparing with words, always knowing where the spirit wind will blow tomorrow. The cloth seller, people say, grew rich and never slept upstairs again.
kultivator.lore.kota_besar.awan.judul: The Cloud District: A Harbour for the Sky
kultivator.lore.kota_besar.cendekia.1: Every sect that swore upon the stone of the square must leave a copy of its founding manual in the Grand Library. Its shelves now hold the learning of more than forty sects, including sects long gone. No sect can attack the capital without burning its own knowledge.
kultivator.lore.kota_besar.cendekia.2: The librarians swear never to open the books they guard except to recopy a crumbling page. The public reading room holds only mortal books: history, medicine, astronomy, law. There is a lecture every day for those who can sit still; people say insight comes to the patient listener, not the clever asker.
kultivator.lore.kota_besar.cendekia.3: In the cellar stands one empty shelf that has never been filled. It is for the eighth sect, says the eldest librarian, "which is not yet born and will surely come." He has never explained how he knows.
kultivator.lore.kota_besar.cendekia.judu: The Scholars' District: Shelves Stronger than Walls
kultivator.lore.kota_besar.cendekia.sumb: Source: Inspired by the Siku Quanshu, the great Qing-dynasty compilation that was copied seven times and kept in seven library pavilions; this library and its oath are game design.
kultivator.lore.kota_besar.gerbang.1: The south gate is the city's mouth. Behind it run inns, teahouses and Lantern Street, where newcomers first smell the city: tea, horse sweat and incense. The gate guards, people say, can tell where someone comes from by the dust on their shoes.
kultivator.lore.kota_besar.gerbang.2: The drum on the gate tower is struck twelve times each night. After the last beat the gate closes, and those left outside must plead with the guard or sleep in the Caravan Field. Many of the city's love stories began beneath a gate that had just shut.
kultivator.lore.kota_besar.gerbang.judul: The Gate District: Inns and Lanterns
kultivator.lore.kota_besar.gilda.1: The Alchemist Guild, the Forge Guild and the Cultivators' Guild rose with the city, and they have quarrelled since the first day: who served best, who pays most, who owns the well in the middle of the district. The well is still there, ringed by three different fences.
kultivator.lore.kota_besar.gilda.2: That quarrel is what keeps the city. The guild council chooses the Warden Prince, and since the three guilds never easily agree on one man, no prince can rule too long without the people's favour. The merchants call it "the three-legged scale": wobbly, but it never falls.
kultivator.lore.kota_besar.gilda.judul: The Guild District: Three Guilds, One Quarrel
The western ward houses craftsmen, scribes, guild servants and cultivator families who chose a mortal life. The houses face inward around four-sided courtyards, their walls high and their doors turned south; a child can grow up here without ever seeing a drawn blade.

Each lane has a lane head who records who moves in and who is born. The mothers say they fear the lane head more than the magistrate, because the magistrate knows only the law and the lane head knows everything.
The West Residences: Houses Behind Walls
kultivator.lore.kota_besar.istana.1: The Warden Prince's palace was once the shared fortress of the seven sects, where the masters kept hostages from one another so no one would betray the rest. Its seven watchtowers still stand; each was raised by one sect with its own stone, so no two towers share a colour.
kultivator.lore.kota_besar.istana.2: The last hostage was freed four hundred years ago, and the cells became audience halls. Honoured guests are still served in the hall where the hostages once ate, from the same bowls. The ministers say it reminds everyone how close hospitality sits to threat.
kultivator.lore.kota_besar.istana.3: Anyone who enters after the night drum without standing in this city is held, even with a sect's letter in hand. The palace guards know no friend or foe; they know only the hour.
kultivator.lore.kota_besar.istana.judul: The Palace District: A Fortress Turned Home
kultivator.lore.kota_besar.judul: The Capital: Neutral Ground of the Seven Sects
kultivator.lore.kota_besar.kumuh.1: Outside the east wall the shacks crowd together like birds' nests. Most of those who live there fled villages overrun by spirit beasts; they came to the capital for its walls, then found the walls were not built for them.
kultivator.lore.kota_besar.kumuh.2: The slums have their own law. No one steals from the common kitchen, no one reports a neighbour to the guards, and everyone knows the old beggar who sleeps by the well is no ordinary beggar, though no one has ever seen him do anything remarkable.
kultivator.lore.kota_besar.kumuh.3: Beneath the pawnshop at the end of the lane, people say, there is a market that opens only when the candles go out. The guards know, but the guards also need medicine the East Market does not sell.
kultivator.lore.kota_besar.kumuh.judul: The Slums: Those Who Came After the Beasts
kultivator.lore.kota_besar.luar.1: South of the gate spreads the field where caravans camp, horses drink and loads are weighed before the gate tax is paid. The distance post at its edge records how many li it is to every great town a caravan from here has ever reached.
kultivator.lore.kota_besar.luar.2: At the Farewell Pavilion people see off relatives on long journeys with a cup of wine and a willow sprig. The sprigs are planted at the field's edge; the row of old willows there is now thousands of farewells grown into trees.
kultivator.lore.kota_besar.luar.judul: The Caravan Field: A Town Outside the Town
kultivator.lore.kota_besar.luar.sumber: Source: Inspired by the Tang custom of breaking a willow sprig (zhe liu) to see off someone leaving on a long journey, as at the Ba Bridge outside Chang'an; the field and its trees are game design.
kultivator.lore.kota_besar.pasar.1: Before there was a wall there was House Qian. The family of stone changers traded at the road post where the seven sects would later make peace, and through the war they lent spirit stones to all sides at once. When peace came every sect was in their debt, and none dared tell them to move.
kultivator.lore.kota_besar.pasar.2: The East Market grew around the Money House the way a town grows around a well. Every night the night market lights its lanterns, and every seventh day the Auction House calls collectors from across the world. Merchants say everything here has a price; only time cannot be haggled.
kultivator.lore.kota_besar.pasar.judul: The East Market: A Money House Older than the City
kultivator.lore.kota_besar.pasar.sumber: Source: Inspired by the East and West Markets of Tang-dynasty Chang'an and the Shanxi remittance houses (piaohao) of the Qing dynasty; House Qian and its history are game design.
kultivator.lore.kota_besar.pusat.1: In the middle of the Grand Square stands the Founders' Monument: a black boulder three men tall with seven broken swords set into it. The swords do not rust, though nine hundred years of rain have soaked them. The alchemists say it is their spirit iron; the monks say it is the oath.
kultivator.lore.kota_besar.pusat.2: On the north side of the square stands the Yamen, where the city magistrate weighs cases under the three laws: swords sleep within the walls, debts are paid and promises kept, the gates close after the night drum. The wanted board before it is rarely empty. People say the Yamen painter has never drawn a face wrong.
kultivator.lore.kota_besar.pusat.3: On every anniversary of the oath the sect envoys lay a stick of incense at the foot of the monument. When a sect fails to come, everyone in the city knows the year will be hard.
kultivator.lore.kota_besar.pusat.judul: The Central District: The Founders' Monument
kultivator.lore.kota_besar.sumber: Source: Inspired by the neutral cities where every sect trades and competes in xianxia novels, such as the Central Plains (Zhongzhou) of Battle Through the Heavens; the nine-hundred-year history and the oath of the seven sects are game design.
kultivator.lore.situs.mata_air_roh.1: By rivers and in quiet woods water sometimes rises from jade rock with qi strong enough to taste. Locals build a small shrine beside it and ask people to drink only once a day; the greedy, they say, find it tastes like ordinary water.
kultivator.lore.situs.mata_air_roh.2: Alchemists value this water above gold, for the finest antidotes cannot be brewed with well water. In the capital, Elder Dan Chen keeps a jar of spirit spring water under his desk and never lends it.
kultivator.lore.situs.panggung_bintang.1: On a high meadow stands a round stage with crossing bronze rings: an old armillary built by sky watchers before the sects existed. No hand ever turns its rings, yet on nights of heavenly events, people say, they move by themselves to follow the stars.
kultivator.lore.situs.panggung_bintang.2: The watchers believed a star calamity is a test, not a punishment, and that whoever faces it beneath the armillary is rewarded more by heaven. No one knows whether that is true, but no one wants to be the first to prove it wrong.
kultivator.lore.situs.panggung_bintang.s: Source: Inspired by ancient Chinese armillary spheres, such as the water-driven armillary built by Zhang Heng in the Eastern Han dynasty; the stage and its beliefs are game design.
kultivator.lore.situs.puncak_petir.1: On the highest peaks nine copper pillars stand around an altar terrace. It is said the copper draws off some of heaven's anger, so a tribulation faced here is a little lighter. Many cultivators climb for days just to break through at this place.
kultivator.lore.situs.puncak_petir.2: The Record Stone in the middle of the terrace keeps the name of everyone who survived a tribulation here, with their realm and day. Wanderers like to come and watch; they say seeing someone else forged by heaven is the cheapest way to learn humility.
kultivator.lore.situs.puncak_petir.judul: Thunder Peak: The Stone of Tribulations
kultivator.lore.situs.puncak_petir.sumbe: Source: Inspired by the heavenly lightning tribulation (tianjie) cultivators must pass when breaking through in xianxia novels; the copper pillars and the Record Stone are game design.
kultivator.lore.ui.belum: You have not heard that tale yet. Visit the place first.
kultivator.lore.ui.kosong: You know no place's tale yet. Visit cities, villages, caves and roads; listen when people talk.
